sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 6 guntas of Sompura village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka has L.A.C. No.267/2002 been acquired for the purpose of extension of Banashankari 6th stage.
Preliminary notification was published in the Gazette on 01.12.2000.
The final notification has been published in the Gazette on 23.08.2001.
the L.A.O. has passed the award on 30.10.2001.

The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.
4,26,286/- per acre in-respect of dry land and Rs. 4,68,915/- in-respect of garden land.

As there was a dispute with regard to title, the L.A.O. has sent the reference and has deposited a sum of Rs.
2,13,143/-.

The said amount has been kept in the Indian Overseas Bank, TKV Extension counter,
Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notice to both parties.
In pursuance of notice, both parties had entered appearance through their counsel.
.4. The claimant No. 3 Venkatarasappa has filed claim statement stating that the propositor Venkataramanappa and his sons constitute Hindu undivided co-parcenary joint family.

It is stated that he and his son have filed a suit in O.S.No. 957/2001 on L.A.C. No.267/2002 the file of Civil Judge (Sr.Dvn), Bengaluru for partition and separate possession of the aforesaid properties and they have claimed 1/4th share in all the aforesaid properties.
The aforesaid properties have been notified by the respondents for the purpose of acquisition of land for formation of layout Banashankari 6th stage.

sentences.text:
The claimant No. 4 M. Puttaswamy has filed claim statement stating that the land bearing Sy.No.
28/24 measuring 9 guntas of Sompura village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka originally belongs to Galappa and the said land was purchased by his father G. Muniswamaiah through a registered sale deed on 08.05.1974.
It is stated that from the day of purchase his father was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property.
His father died on 08.05.1985 and after his death, he was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property till its acquisition.
It is stated that all the revenue records, encumbrance stands in his name.
The L.A.O. has given endorsement to this claimant on L.A.C. No.267/2002 10.12.2002 stating that the amount pertaining to above acquisition has been deposited before this Court.
Hence prayed pass an award/ compensation in his favour.
.6. In order to prove their case, the claimant No. 4 has been examined as PW.1.
The General Power of Attorney holder of claimant No. 3 has been examined as PW.2.
The documents marked at Ex.P.1 to 26.
.7. Heard the arguments.

.8. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1. Which of the claimants are entitled for compensation amount disputed in this case?
2. What order or award?

.9. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: As per discussion Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .10.
Point No.1:
The claimant No.4 M. Puttaswamy has been examined as PW.1.
He has stated L.A.C. No.267/2002 that the land bearing Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas situated at Sompura village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka originally belonged to Galappa.

The said land was purchased by his father G.
Muniswamaiah under a registered sale deed dated 08.05.1974.

Ex.P.1 is the sale deed which discloses that the sale made by Galappa in-favour of G. Muniswamaiah in-respect of Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas along with Sy.No. 27/6 measuring 32 guntas out of 1 acre 31 guntas.
PW. 1 has stated that from the date of purchase, his father was in possession and enjoyment of the property till his death.
PW. 1 has stated that his father died on 08.05.1984 and after the death of his father, he has been in possession and enjoyment of the property till acquisition.
PW. 1 has stated that all the revenue records stand in his name and he is the only son of his father.

Hence, he has prayed for compensation.
.11.
To corroborate his contention, he has produced Ex.P.2 Encumbrance certificate for the period from 01.06.1989 to 01.01.2002, which discloses nil L.A.C. No.267/2002 encumbrance.
Ex. P.3
is the form No. 16.
From the said document, it is seen that Galappa has sold Sy.No. 28/4 along with other properties measuring 9 guntas in- favour of G. Muniswamaiah under a sale deed No. 1385/74-75.

From the document, it is seen that Narasimhaiah S/o Galappa had filed the case against Assistant Commissioner, Special Tahsildar and claimant No. 4 challenging the order passed by the Assistant Commissioner No. RA(S)76/2002-03 dated 26.06.2003.
The Deputy Commissioner had confirmed the order of the Assistant Commissioner and Revision petition was dismissed.
Ex.P.6 is the endorsement given by SLAO to to claimant No. 4.
Ex.P.7 is the RTC Extract for the year 2005-06, name of claimant No. 4 is mentioned at Col. No. 9 and 12(2) and the name has been entered in pursuance to pouti.
During cross-examination he pleads ignorance as in whose name khatha stood.
In Ex.P.7 RTC Extract name of Galappa has not been mentioned.
He admits that he has not produced the mutation made in his favour in-respect of acquired land.
He admits that he has not produced copy of objection filed before the L.A.O.
he pleads ignorance as to Ex.P.3, in whose name khatha stood.
He pleads ignorance as to whether Galappa had sold the property to any other persons and about the fact that on 06.11.1963 Galappa had sold Sy.No. 28/24 in-favour of D. Arasappa.
He pleads ignorance when it is suggested that property was sold by Galappa in-favour of his father.
The khatha stood in the name of D. Arasappa.
He pleads ignorance when it is suggested that Galappa had no right to execute the sale deed dated 08.05.1974 as he did not have any title.

He has stated that in the year 2001 the B.D.A. had taken possession of the land and pleads ignorance when it is suggested that Venkatarasappa had filed a suit in L.A.C. No.267/2002 O.S.No. 957/2001 for partition and separate possession of 1/4th share.
.13. The General Power of Attorney holder of claimant No. 3 i.e., Mahadevappa has been examined as PW.2.
He has produced General Power of Attorney executed in his favour as per Ex.P.8.
PW.2 has stated that the land bearing Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas was purchased by his uncle Arasappa under a sale deed dated 06.11.1963 from Galappa as member of the joint Hindu family.
He has stated that his uncle and he were in joint possession of the said property.
As the sale deed was in the name of his uncle, the record of right has been entered in the name of his uncle D. Arasappa.
The mutation was accepted in the name of his uncle as per sale deed.
.14. PW.2 has stated that he and his father filed O.S.No. 957/2001 for partition and separate possession of the joint family properties.
In the said suit, the property bearing Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas of Sompura village was also the subject matter of the suit.
The suit came to be decreed.

Thereafter the defendants had filed RFA No.
2608/2007 and the interim stay was granted by this Court.
He has stated that the property bearing Sy.No. 28/24 was correctly mentioned in para No. 4 of the plaint.
However, at the time of filing the amended plaint the property bearing Sy.No. 28/24 has been mentioned as Sy.No. 28/2A.
The said mistake was bonafide and not intentional.
After the judgment the said mistake could not be carried out.
As the judgment and decree was questioned in RFA No.2608/2007 he was not able to rectify the said mistake in the judgment and decree.
.15. PW.2 has denied that father of claimant No. 4 had purchased Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas from G. Muniswamaiah.

He has stated that there is no mutation in-respect of property in-favour of ) Arasappa vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 10 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24073456/

sentences.text: The claimant No. 4 has obtained mutation entry without making claimant No. 3 as party to the proceeding.
So, the claimant No. 4 has no right to claim right, title and interest in-respect of the land L.A.C. No.267/2002 bearing Sy.No. 28/24.
He has stated that by virtue of the decree passed in O.S.No. 957/2001, the claimant No. 3 and other were entitled to receive the compensation.

The claimant No. 3 is entitled for 1/4th share in Sy.No. 28/24 along with others, as claimant No. 4 has no right to claim compensation in-respect of property bearing Sy.No.
28/24.

It is stated that claimant No. 4 without disclosing the fact that the khatha was standing in the name of D. Arasappa, in collusion with Revenue authorities, has got entered his name without notice to D. Arasappa and his legal heirs.

PW.2 has stated that claimant No. 4 is aware about RFA No.2608/2007.
.16.
It is stated that after the death of his father claimant No. 3, claimant No. 3(a) to 3(f) have been impleaded as parties to the claim petition.

It is stated that the RFA No. 2608/2007 was pending before the Hon'ble High Court; that on 15.02.2011 the compromise petition was accepted by the Hon'ble High Court and judgment and decree was passed.
In view of pendency L.A.C. No.267/2002 of the proceedings with regard to the aforesaid land, the said land was not allotted in favour of any one and it has been kept open to the parties.
So, he and other members of the family are equally entitled to claim compensation amount.
.17. In support of his contention, PW.2 has relied upon the following documents.
Ex.P.9 is the plaint in O.S.No.957/2001 filed by claimant No. 3 and his son against claimants 5 to 11, 15 and 17.

Item No.
23 is an agricultural land in Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas of Sompura village.
The advocate for the claimant No. 3 has submitted that in the amended plaint filed by them item No. 24 was wrongly typed as Sy.No. 28/2A instead of 28/24.
Ex.P.10 is the judgment.
As per the judgment, it is held that the plaintiffs are entitled for 1/4th share in the suit schedule properties.
In the decree, Sl.No. 23 pertain to Sy.No. 28/2A.
Ex.P.11 is the order in RFA No. 2608/2007.
It discloses that the order in O.S.No. 957/2001 has been stayed.
Ex.P.12 is the Genealogical tree of family of Venkataramanappa.
L.A.C. No.267/2002 Ex.P.13 is the sale deed dated 06.11.1963.

From the sale deed it is seen that Galappa has executed a sale deed in-favour of D. Arasappa S/o Veerachikkappa in- respect of Sy.No.
28/24 measuring to an extent of 9 guntas of Sompura village.
.18.

Ex.P.14 to 18 are the RTC Extracts for the year from 1984 to 2001 in-respect of Sy.No. 28/24,
name of Arasappa has entered in Col. No.9 and 12(2).
Ex.P.19 to 21 are the RTC Extracts for the period from 1969 to 1984 in-respect of Sy.No. 28/24 name of Arasappa is mentioned at Col. No. 9 and 12(2).
Ex.P.22 is the Encumbrance certificate for the period from 01.04.1963 to 31.05.1989.
From the document, it is seen that Galappa has executed a sale deed dated 06.11.1963 in-favour of D. Arasappa to an extent of 9 guntas in Sy.No. 28/24 of Sompura village.

Ex.P.23 is the nil encumbrance for the period from 01.06.1989 to 31.03.2002.
.19.
During cross-examination PW.2 has stated that original document Ex.P.13 was with his senior L.A.C. No.267/2002 uncle and after his death, he does not know in whose name property stood.
With regard to the acquired land, he has stated that the property stood in the name of his senior uncle Arasappa.
He has produced Genealogical tree to prove that he is in joint family.

Though PW.2 ) Arasappa vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 10 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24073456/
8 has been cross-examined nothing substantial has been elicited to disbelieve his evidence.

sentences.text: .20. From the oral and documentary evidence, it is seen that the total extent of Sy.No.28/24 is 9 guntas.
Arasappa had purchased the property bearing Sy.No. 28/24 under a sale deed dated 06.11.1963 from Galappa measuring 9 guntas.
Galappa had sold to Arasappa the entire extent.
So he did not have title to execute the sale deed to an extent of 9 guntas in favour of G. Muniswamaiah.

Even though the said Galappa had executed the sale deed dated 08.05.1974 in-favour of G.
Muniswamaiah, G. Muniswamaiah does not acquire any title as Galappa did not have title or possession to convey to Muniswamaiah.
There is no document produced by PW.1 to show that L.A.C. No.267/2002 Muniswamaiah was in possession of Sy.No. 28/24.
Except RTC for the year 2004-2005 in the name of PW.1 which is subsequent to acquisition there is no other document with regard to possession.
On the other hand, the material before this Court discloses that Arasappa was in possession of Sy.No. 28/24 till acquisition.
Hence, it is held that by virtue of sale deed and since Arasappa was in possession he is owner of the property.
As per Ex.P.9 it is seen that acquired property is joint family property.
The claimant No. 3 is entitled for 1/4th share in the suit schedule properties.

The defendants being aggrieved by the said judgment, had filed appeal in RFA No.
2608/2007.
The said appeal was compromised.

At para No. 11 it is mentioned that in view of acquisition of all the suit schedule properties except house property in Sy.No. ---- by B.D.A. and KIADB the reference under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act, is pending before the Civil Court.
The parties are entitled to claim compensation and other benefits as per law to the extent of properties allotted under this L.A.C. No.267/2002 compromise petition.
From the compromise petition, it is seen that Sy.No. 27/24 has not been specifically allotted to any body.
The claimants are claiming 1/4th share.

From the judgment, it is clear that at para No. 27 it has been held that the suit schedule properties are the joint family properties and that the plaintiffs being LRs of Muddappa are together entitled to get 1/4th share in the suit schedule properties.

In view of the said judgment, claimant No.
3 and his son Mahadevappa are together entitled for 1/4th share in Sy.No. 28/24.
In view of death of claimant No.3 his legal heirs are entitled for compensation in respect of the 1/4th share in 6 guntas.
The award discloses that 6 guntas of land are reserved kharab.
The claimants 1, 2, 5 to 19 though had entered appearance did not file claim statement.
So their claim is reflected.
Hence, point No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
.21. Point No.2:

In view of my finding on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
L.A.C. No.267/2002 O R DE R
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO, KIADB (BMICP), Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby partly allowed.
LRs of claimant No.3 are together entitled for 1/4th share in 6 guntas of land in-respect of Sy.No.28/24 of Sompura village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka along with accrued interest thereon.

The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bonds with one surety each,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.

Preliminary notification was published in the Gazette on 01.12.2000.

opennyai_summary.issue:
.8. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1. Which of the claimants are entitled for compensation amount disputed in this case?
2. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Deputy Commissioner had confirmed the order of the Assistant Commissioner and Revision petition was dismissed.
As the sale deed was in the name of his uncle, the record of right has been entered in the name of his uncle D. Arasappa.
The mutation was accepted in the name of his uncle as per sale deed.
In the said suit, the property bearing Sy.No. 28/24 measuring 9 guntas of Sompura village was also the subject matter of the suit.
The suit came to be decreed.
The said mistake was bonafide and not intentional.
After the judgment the said mistake could not be carried out.
So, the claimant No. 4 has no right to claim right, title and interest in-respect of the land L.A.C. No.267/2002 bearing Sy.No. 28/24.
Arasappa had purchased the property bearing Sy.No. 28/24 under a sale deed dated 06.11.1963 from Galappa measuring 9 guntas.
Galappa had sold to Arasappa the entire extent.
So he did not have title to execute the sale deed to an extent of 9 guntas in favour of G. Muniswamaiah.
Even though the said Galappa had executed the sale deed dated 08.05.1974 in-favour of G.
Muniswamaiah, G. Muniswamaiah does not acquire any title as Galappa did not have title or possession to convey to Muniswamaiah.
There is no document produced by PW.1 to show that L.A.C. No.267/2002 Muniswamaiah was in possession of Sy.No. 28/24.
Except RTC for the year 2004-2005 in the name of PW.1 which is subsequent to acquisition there is no other document with regard to possession.
On the other hand, the material before this Court discloses that Arasappa was in possession of Sy.No. 28/24 till acquisition.
Hence, it is held that by virtue of sale deed and since Arasappa was in possession he is owner of the property.
The claimant No. 3 is entitled for 1/4th share in the suit schedule properties.
The defendants being aggrieved by the said judgment, had filed appeal in RFA No.
2608/2007.
The said appeal was compromised.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, point No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
.21. Point No.2:
In view of my finding on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
L.A.C. No.267/2002 O R DE R
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO, KIADB (BMICP), Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby partly allowed.
LRs of claimant No.3 are together entitled for 1/4th share in 6 guntas of land in-respect of Sy.No.28/24 of Sompura village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka along with accrued interest thereon.
The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bonds with one surety each,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The above claimants are entitled to interest under Section 34 of the L.A. Act.
The amount already paid by L.A.O., has to be deducted.
Claim against claimant No. 4 is dismissed.
Claim against claimants 1, 2, 5 to 19 is rejected.
